references.text: The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 6:30|Matthew 6:30] contains the same teaching from Jesus that if God clothes the grass of the field, how much more will He clothe you, O you of little faith. The wording is almost identical.
The immediate context in [ref:Luk 12:22-27|Luke 12:22-27] provides the background for Jesus' exhortation not to worry about clothes and food, using examples of ravens and lilies.

[ref:Sal 103:15-16|Psalm 103:15-16] describes human transience as grass of the field: "A person's days are like grass; they flourish like a flower of the field. When the wind passes over it, it is gone." This is the same basic imagery about the fleeting existence of grass that Jesus uses.

[ref:Jes 40:6-8|Isaiah 40:6-8] compares all flesh to grass and its glory to the flower of the field that withers – the same motif Jesus uses to illustrate that God still gives beauty to the grass, and how much more will He provide for His children.
[ref:Jak 1:10-11|James 1:10-11] uses the same image of grass and a flower that withers in the heat of the sun to illustrate transience.

[ref:1 Pet 1:24-25|1 Peter 1:24-25] quotes Isaiah 40 that all flesh is like grass and its glory like the flower of grass – it withers and the flower falls off. This emphasizes the same image of the transience of grass.

The entire passage in [ref:Matt 6:25-34|Matthew 6:25-34] is the parallel to Jesus' teaching on not worrying, where He uses the argument from the lesser to the greater (a fortiori): God cares for the grass, how much more for you.
[ref:Matt 8:26|Matthew 8:26] uses the expression "you of little faith" (ὀλιγόπιστοι), the same rare word Jesus uses in Luke 12:28 to rebuke the disciples' lack of faith.

[ref:Matt 14:31|Matthew 14:31] also uses "little faith" (ὀλιγόπιστε) when Jesus speaks to Peter who is sinking in the water. It shows Jesus' repeated use of this expression to challenge the disciples to greater faith.

[ref:Matt 16:8|Matthew 16:8] is another occurrence of "you of little faith" (ὀλιγόπιστοι), where Jesus rebukes the disciples for worrying about bread. The theme is the same: God provides for material needs.
